question.text: Tangent is drawn at any point $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y})$ on a curve, which passes through $(1,1)$. The tangent cuts X-axis and Y-axis at A and B respectively. If AP:BP = 3:1, then

options.text: the differential equation of the curve is $3 \mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\mathrm{y}=0$
the differential equation of the curve is $3 \mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}-\mathrm{y}=0$

solution.text:
Hint:
$\frac{P A}{P B}=\frac{3}{1}$ Equation of tangent $\mathrm{AB}$ is $\mathrm{Y}-\mathrm{y}=\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}}(\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{x})$ $\mathrm{A}\left(\frac{\mathrm{xy}^{\prime}-\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{y}^{\prime}}, 0\right)$ and $\mathrm{B}\left(0, \mathrm{y}-\mathrm{xy}^{\prime}\right)$ Using section formula : $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1 \times 0+3 \times\left(\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{xy}^{\prime}\right)}{4} \Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{y}=3 \mathrm{y}-3 \mathrm{xy}^{\prime} \Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{xy}^{\prime}=-\mathrm{y} \Rightarrow \frac{3 \mathrm{xdy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\mathrm{y}=0$ $\frac{3 d y}{y}+\frac{d x}{x}=0$ $\mathrm{xy}^{3}=1$ $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}_{(1,1)}}=\frac{-1}{3}$ Slope of Normal $=3$ Equation of Normal $\Rightarrow y-1=3(x-1) \Rightarrow y-3 x+2=0$
